question: Using only the indexed RBI priority-sector lending directions for scheduled commercial banks, small finance banks (SFBs) and regional rural banks (RRBs), assess a group's plan to apply a common 40% total priority-sector target and 10% weaker-sections target to all three bank types. (1) Compare total priority sector, agriculture, small and marginal farmers, micro-enterprises and weaker-sections targets, keeping each bank type and denominator distinct. (2) Calculate the total priority-sector minimum for a domestic scheduled commercial bank with ANBC of Rs 1,000 crore and credit-equivalent off-balance-sheet exposure of Rs 1,200 crore, an SFB with ANBC of Rs 1,000 crore, and an RRB with total outstanding advances of Rs 800 crore, using the applicable measurement date. (3) State which parts of the common plan fail for each bank type. Cite all three indexed directions; do not substitute later rules.
notes: Reviewed bank-specific rates and denominators on commercial-bank PDF p4, SFB p3 and RRB p3. Different scopes are not a source conflict. Manually verify every bank/rate/calculation association.

question: Using the indexed RBI Currency Distribution & Exchange Scheme (CDES) and currency-chest penal-interest circular, assess a currency chest in an underbanked North Eastern town with 80,000 people. Its eligible capital expenditure is Rs 80 lakh and annual eligible revenue expenditure is Rs 10 lakh. (1) Calculate the capital reimbursement and annual revenue reimbursement and duration, and compare with the same chest outside the North East. (2) Give the incentive rates and units for soiled notes of denomination Rs 50 or less, mutilated notes and retail coin distribution, including how coin incentives are paid. (3) State the minimum deposit/withdrawal amount, increments, reporting channel and deadline, and ordinary penal-interest rate. (4) Explain how a late net-deposit report is treated differently from wrong reporting, and whether a first-time clerical error justifies waiver. Cite both circulars and preserve discretionary wording.
notes: CDES PDF pp2-3; penalty PDF pp2,4. Manually check capital cap, 50% revenue periods, rates/units, may-not-charge interest/may-levy flat Rs50000, and wrong-reporting waiver exclusion.

question: Using the indexed SEBI Master Circulars for Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs) and listed entities under LODR, assess this shared complaint-reporting plan. An RTA proposes to publish its March 2026 complaints and redressal data on its website on 30 April, claiming the listed issuer's quarterly deadline covers it. The listed issuer proposes to file its Integrated Filing (Governance), including investor-grievance redressal, for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 on 30 April. (1) State each entity's obligation, frequency, deadline and whether its proposed date meets that deadline. (2) Explain which complaints the RTA must disclose and how it must bring its Investor Charter to existing and new shareholders, including RAIN's role. (3) Explain whether these different deadlines contradict one another or apply to different duties. Cite both circulars.
notes: RTA PDF p64, LODR pp52-53. RTA March publication due April7; listed entity quarter filing due April30. No conflict: monthly RTA website obligation and quarterly listed-issuer filing have distinct applicability.

question: Using the indexed RBI NBFC Acceptance of Public Deposits Direction and RBI KYC Direction, assess an otherwise eligible investment and credit company with net owned funds of Rs 10 crore. It proposes aggregate outstanding public deposits of Rs 18 crore, nine-month deposits, and deposits repayable on demand. Its corporate customer has one natural person owning 12% of shares and another natural person owning no shares but holding the contractual right to appoint a majority of directors. (1) Calculate the maximum aggregate public deposits and assess the proposed Rs 18 crore. (2) Give the permitted maturity range and assess the nine-month and demand-repayment proposals. (3) State the company's beneficial-ownership test and explain whether each natural person qualifies, keeping ownership and control through other means distinct. Cite both indexed directions and do not substitute later rules.
notes: NBFC PDF p12: demand prohibition,12-60months,aggregate1.5NOF. KYC PDF p5: company BO ownership morethan10% or control including majority-director appointment. Both persons qualify. Manual check scope and explicit scenario verdicts.

question: Using the SEBI Master Circulars for Investment Advisers and Research Analysts dated 6 February 2026, assess this plan for a partnership firm registered as both an IA and an RA. Its peak client counts in the previous financial year were 280 advisory clients and 425 research clients; it currently has only 120 clients in each business. For an ordinary, non-accredited individual client family, it proposes fixed annual fees of Rs 160,000 for investment advice and Rs 160,000 for research, excluding statutory charges. It wants to collect 18 months of fees upfront and retain three months of fees if either contract is terminated early. It also wants to operate advisory and research as one undifferentiated service. Explain: (1) the dual-registration compliance and segregation requirements; (2) the annual fee ceiling and maximum advance period for each service; (3) how refunds and breakage fees differ between IA and RA; (4) the deposit required for each registration, the lien beneficiary, which client counts determine the deposit, and the deadline for updating it; and (5) which fee rules change for corporate clients or accredited investors. Cite both circulars and distinguish their rules.
notes: Compare both roles, apply prior-year peaks, retain required undertaking, and disclose main-rule/MITC advance-fee discrepancy.
